notes:
Scope: every runtime HTTP call in the desktop client. 18 api.request call sites (grep of src: app.ts x12, Composer.tsx x2, Inspector.tsx, CommandPalette.tsx, ChatArea.tsx, SidePanels.tsx, SettingsPanel.tsx, Sidebar.tsx), plus the Rust-side direct calls /health (runtime.rs:216), /v1/runtime/info (runtime.rs:234) and the SSE stream (api.rs:129). ollama.rs and system.rs only talk to Ollama (/api/version, /api/ps, /api/tags, /api/show, /api/create, /api/generate at ollama.rs:38-162), never the runtime. No fetch/EventSource exists in src. No files were edited.

Overall: request field names and casing match the server on every endpoint. All snake_case, except image inputs, which are camelCase {mime,dataBase64} with deny_unknown_fields (protocol/src/runtime/mod.rs:17-22). The client matches that exactly after Composer.tsx:212 strips `name`. Auth is also correct: Bearer header and env var name match (api.rs:66 vs runtime_api/auth.rs:138-143; runtime.rs:161 vs runtime_api.rs:144,1901-1906). The error envelope /error/message matches too (api.rs:77 vs runtime_api.rs:12865-12887). So nothing is "broken" at the wire level.

Real defects, in priority order:
1. MAJOR (threads.ts:217-218): stream.progress has `state` at the top level (runtime_api.rs:9124-9135), not under `payload`, so ThreadView.live is never true. Auto-approve is fully dead (useBootstrap.ts:17), and a new or empty thread renders a skeleton forever (MessageList.tsx:75). Fix: read ev.state for this event (or (ev as any).payload?.state ?? (ev as any).state).
2. MAJOR (api.rs:129): replay_limit=4096 means "last 4096 events", not "batch size" (runtime_threads.rs:4450-4481), and per-token item.delta events are persisted, so history of long threads is silently truncated on open. Suggested fix: GET /v1/threads/{id} (ThreadDetail: turns, items, pending_approvals, latest_seq; runtime_threads.rs:5284-5309), hydrate the store, then subscribe with since_seq=latest_seq and no replay_limit. Alternatively, drop replay_limit, or detect gaps via previous_seq.
3. MINOR: latest_turn_status is Debug-lowercased ("inprogress", runtime_threads.rs:10481-10482), but Sidebar.tsx:81 checks "in_progress". Compare against "inprogress"/"queued", or normalize by removing underscores.
4. MINOR: the runtime never emits turn.failed/turn.interrupted/turn.canceled; everything is turn.completed plus turn.status (runtime_threads.rs:9703-9731, 18712). Derive lastError from p.turn.status==="failed" on turn.completed.
5. MINOR (perf): useBootstrap.ts:33-38 calls refreshThreads and refreshContext on every replayed turn.completed. Opening a thread with N turns fires about 3N requests, and each summary call spawns git processes (runtime_api.rs:3290-3305). Gate it on t.live (after fix 1) or debounce it.
6. MINOR: in ContextInfo (types.ts:97-111), provider/pressure are typed non-null but can be null (context.rs:20,33,80-94), and model_provider_id is missing. Inspector.tsx:193 should also warn on "critical" (context_budget.rs:118-120).
7. MINOR: /v1/usage `turns` counts provider calls, not user turns (runtime_threads.rs:5423-5425).
8. Cosmetic: the file search returns files only (workspace.rs:80), so the dir icon at Composer.tsx:181 never appears. operation_key is regenerated per call (app.ts:208), so idempotent retry (runtime_api.rs:8477-8484) is never used.

Startup/process facts:
- `app-server --http --host --port` is forwarded to `serve --http --host --port` (cli/src/lib.rs:6266-6276). The default port would be 7878 (lib.rs:6227-6235), but the client always passes a free port.
- If an owner runtime is already published (e.g. a TUI started from PowerShell), the new process attaches as a listener frontend of that owner instead of opening its own store (runtime_api.rs:1766-1835). Same HTTP contract, but threads and workspace are the owner's.
- Upstream has no `codewhale-app-server` binary: crates/app-server is a library (Cargo.toml:2), and the only bin is `codewhale` (crates/cli/Cargo.toml:22-23). The externalBin binaries/codewhale-app-server (src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:34) must therefore be a renamed `codewhale` binary. That works, because runtime.rs:159 passes the `app-server` subcommand.
- /health and /v1/runtime/info are intentionally unauthenticated (runtime_api.rs:2842-2848). /v1/runtime/info has no request timeout (runtime.rs:234).

verdict.evidence:
The claim holds. I could not refute it.

Request side:
- The client sends GET /v1/threads/summary?limit=300 (src/store/app.ts:137) and filters `!s.archived` (app.ts:141). This works.
- All field names in the TS ThreadSummary (src/lib/types.ts:32-47) match the server struct ThreadSummary (cw-src/crates/tui/src/runtime_api.rs:988-1007).
- The server struct is a plain `#[derive(Serialize)]` with no rename, so its keys are snake_case.

Response side, where the mismatch is:
- In the summary handler, `latest_turn_status` is copied unchanged from `facts.latest_turn_status` (runtime_api.rs:3321, 3366). Nothing in the handler normalizes it.
- That fact is built at cw-src/crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs:10481-10482 as `format!("{:?}", turn.status).to_ascii_lowercase()`.
- `turn.status` has type RuntimeTurnStatus (runtime_threads.rs:1491). That enum is `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]` with variants Queued and InProgress (runtime_threads.rs:758-767).
- serde's rename only affects serialization. The code here uses Debug formatting, which prints the Rust variant name "InProgress", and lowercasing gives "inprogress", not "in_progress". The field's doc comment confirms the format: "`Debug`-lowercased for the wire" (runtime_threads.rs:5457).
- Upstream's own web client handles both spellings at cw-src/crates/tui/src/runtime_web/app.mjs:1148: `summary.latest_turn_status === "inprogress" || summary.latest_turn_status === "in_progress"`. This shows "inprogress" is what the server actually sends.

Client effect:
- src/components/layout/Sidebar.tsx:81 checks only `s.latest_turn_status === "in_progress"`. This is the only client read of the field (grep finds only Sidebar.tsx:81 and types.ts:45).
- So the server's running signal never matches. A thread shows as running only if it is subscribed locally and has a local `activeTurnId`. A thread that is running but not open, or one that resumed after the app restarted, shows as idle.
- Queued turns ("queued", from RuntimeTurnStatus::Queued, runtime_threads.rs:760) are also never treated as running. Upstream marks Queued as active work (`is_active_work`, runtime_threads.rs:769-773).

Turn objects elsewhere use serde snake_case "in_progress", so the client's other in_progress checks (Turn.tsx:85, Blocks.tsx) are correct. Only the summary field is affected. Severity "minor" is right: it only affects the sidebar running indicator, not data or control flow.

- The route is `.route("/v1/threads/summary", get(list_threads_summary))` (cw-src/crates/tui/src/runtime_api.rs:2478).

- `limit` is clamped to 1..=500 (runtime_api.rs:3211), so 100 is accepted.
- `search` is ASCII-lowercased (runtime_api.rs:3212). When it is set, the store read is unbounded (`scan_limit = None`, runtime_api.rs:3243-3247), and rows are kept by `thread_matches_summary_search` (runtime_threads.rs:10566-10594), which matches on id, model, the explicit title, or the latest turn's `input_summary`.
- The response is `Json<Vec<ThreadSummary>>` (runtime_api.rs:3210, 3371). The struct (runtime_api.rs:988-1006) derives `Serialize` with no rename_all, so its field names are snake_case. They match the client's `ThreadSummary` (src/lib/types.ts:32-47) one-to-one, including types: `branch`/`head`/`latest_turn_id`/`latest_turn_status` are Option<String> vs string|null, `updated_at` is a chrono DateTime serialized as an ISO string, `workspace` is a PathBuf serialized as a string, and `pending_attention_count` is usize vs number.

Response mismatch (confirmed):
- The server builds `latest_turn_status` as `format!("{:?}", turn.status).to_ascii_lowercase()` (runtime_threads.rs:10481-10482).
- `turn.status` is a `RuntimeTurnStatus` (runtime_threads.rs:1492). That enum derives `Debug` with variants Queued/InProgress/Completed/... (runtime_threads.rs:758-767). Its `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]` affects only serde, not `{:?}`.
- So the wire values are `"queued"`, `"inprogress"`, `"completed"`, `"failed"`, `"interrupted"`, `"canceled"`. They are NOT `"in_progress"`.
- The client checks `s.latest_turn_status === "in_progress"` (Sidebar.tsx:81), which can never be true. The spinner for a thread that is running on the server but not tracked in the local `useThreads` store therefore never shows. That happens after an app reload or runtime reconnect, or for a turn started by the TUI or another client. The client also ignores `"queued"`, which the server counts as active work (runtime_threads.rs:770-773).
- Severity "minor" is fair. It is a UI indicator only, but it is wrong on every row.

Related gaps on the same call (not a parse failure):
1. The search hits are reduced to ids (Sidebar.tsx:228) and only used to filter the already-loaded `summaries` (Sidebar.tsx:245-256). That list comes from `GET /v1/threads/summary?limit=300` (src/store/app.ts:137). The server deliberately scans the whole store so older matches are found (comment at runtime_api.rs:3233-3242), but any hit outside the newest 300 threads is dropped by the client.
2. The server lowercases only ASCII (runtime_api.rs:3212; runtime_threads.rs:10576-10594). A Cyrillic query is case-sensitive on the server. The client's own local filter uses Unicode `toLowerCase` (Sidebar.tsx:246-252).
verdict.fix:
1. Status casing (required), at Sidebar.tsx:81. Normalize before comparing, because the server sends Debug-lowercased names ("inprogress", "queued"), not snake_case:
   `const ts = s.latest_turn_status?.toLowerCase().replace(/[_\s-]/g, "");`
   `const running = useThreads((st) => !!st.threads[s.id]?.activeTurnId) || ts === "inprogress" || ts === "queued";`
   It is better to put this in a shared helper, for example `normTurnStatus()` in src/lib/types.ts, and use it everywhere `latest_turn_status` is read. That keeps the client working if upstream later switches to serde's snake_case `in_progress`. Leave the comparisons on live turn/item `status` values (Turn.tsx:85, Blocks.tsx) as they are; they come from serde-serialized records, which are snake_case.

2. Search results (recommended), at Sidebar.tsx:224-256. Keep the full rows instead of only ids: `const [remoteRows, setRemoteRows] = useState<ThreadSummary[] | null>(null); ... setRemoteRows(res)`. Then build `filtered` as the local matches plus every remote row whose id is not already in `summaries`, skipping `archived`. Matches older than the 300 loaded threads then appear. The request itself can stay exactly as it is: `limit` and `search` bind correctly, and `encodeURIComponent` is right.

3. Optional: for non-ASCII queries, keep the existing client-side Unicode `toLowerCase` filter as the primary matcher. The server matches Cyrillic case-sensitively, so a remote miss there is not a real "no match".

verdict.evidence:
The claim holds. It is a minor type and UI drift, not a broken contract. One citation is wrong: ContextInfo is at src/lib/types.ts:137-151, not 97-111.

Request side (fine)
- The route is GET /v1/threads/{id}/context (crates/tui/src/runtime_api.rs:2527).
- The handler takes only State and Path(thread_id) (context.rs:36-39). There is no query or body extractor.
- The client sends a bare GET to the same path (src/store/app.ts:153).

Response side
- ThreadContextResponse (context.rs:16-34) derives Serialize only, with no rename or skip attributes. Every field is always emitted with its Rust name, and None becomes null.
- Field names match ContextInfo (types.ts:137-151), except that `model_provider_id: Option<String>` (context.rs:21) is missing from the TS type.

Type drift
- `provider` is `Option<String>` (context.rs:20) but TS declares it `provider: string` (types.ts:140).
  - Fallback path: it is `thread.model_provider` (context.rs:83), which is `Option<String>` on ThreadRecord (runtime_threads.rs:812), so it can be null.
  - Live path: it is always Some (context.rs:52), but its value is the literal "unavailable" when the engine has no provider identity (core/engine.rs ~4034-4037).
- `pressure` is `Option<&'static str>` (context.rs:33) but TS declares it `pressure: string` (types.ts:150).
  - It is null on the fallback path (context.rs:94). That path is taken when get_engine fails or get_context_budget returns Ok(None) for a route with no bounded window (engine/handle.rs:784-787).
- Pressure values come from PressureLevel::label (crates/runtime/src/context_budget.rs:115-121): "low", "moderate", "high", "critical". Critical starts at 90% (context_budget.rs:52, 99-100).
- Inspector.tsx:193 sets `warn={ctx?.pressure === "high"}`, so "critical" is shown without the warning color, the worst state looking calmer than "high". The red progress bar is computed separately (Inspector.tsx:155,170), so it still turns red.

Runtime impact today
- No crash. Every consumer null-guards:
  - Inspector.tsx:153-156 and 191-193 use ?? and fmtTokens, which handles null (src/lib/format.ts:1-2).
  - StatusBar.tsx:53-54 uses ??.
  - ChatArea.tsx:67 uses a truthiness check.
- Nothing reads ctx.provider or model_provider_id (grep over src finds no use).
- Fetch errors are swallowed (app.ts:155-157).

Related side effect (not in the claim)
- get_engine calls ensure_engine_loaded (runtime_threads.rs:15893-15896). So every refreshContext call loads the thread's engine: on thread open (app.ts:175, 192, 240) and on the 15 s poll for the active thread (useBootstrap.ts:119-122).
- live:false therefore only appears when that load fails or the route has no bounded window. It does not mean the thread is idle.
verdict.fix:
No change is needed in what the client sends; the GET is correct as is. On the read side, three changes:

1. Update the ContextInfo type in src/lib/types.ts:137-151 to:
   - `provider: string | null;` (and treat "unavailable" as unknown when displaying it)
   - add `model_provider_id: string | null;`
   - `pressure: "low" | "moderate" | "high" | "critical" | null;`
   - keep `live: boolean` and use it in the UI: when `live === false`, show the window size only and render the token, compaction and pressure rows as "unavailable".

2. Change src/components/layout/Inspector.tsx:193 to:
   `warn={ctx?.pressure === "high" || ctx?.pressure === "critical"}`
   Optionally colour "critical" red to match the bar and show translated labels (low, moderate, high, critical) instead of the raw strings.

3. Optional: the server loads the engine when this endpoint is called (runtime_threads.rs:15893-15896). To avoid waking idle threads, poll only while a turn is running or right after a turn finishes, instead of every 15 s (src/hooks/useBootstrap.ts:119-122).

Semantic drift: `turns` counts provider-call usage records incl. child/compaction calls (runtime_threads.rs:5423-5425, 5521-5522), so the "Ходов" tiles over-count user turns

verdict.evidence:
I'm confirming the claim. Its severity is minor: the request and field names work, but the "Ходов" (turns) number counts the wrong thing.

What works:
- Transport. The path `/v1/usage?group_by=day` gets past allowed_path, which only checks the `/v1/` prefix and `..` (src-tauri/src/api.rs:39-41). It is sent as `{base}{path}`, so the query string reaches the server unchanged (api.rs:65).
- Route and query. The route is GET only (cw-src crates/tui/src/runtime_api.rs:2764). UsageQuery uses a plain `#[derive(Deserialize)]` with `since`, `until` and `group_by` all optional, and no renames (runtime_api.rs:10096-10103). get_usage reads it with `Query<UsageQuery>` (runtime_api.rs:10111-10113), and `"day"` maps to UsageGroupBy::Day (runtime_api.rs:10128-10129). With no since or until, the whole history comes back (runtime_api.rs:10114-10121).
- Response shape. The handler returns `json!(aggregation)` (runtime_api.rs:10144-10145). UsageAggregation has `totals: UsageTotals` and `buckets: Vec<UsageBucket>` (runtime_threads.rs:5526-5532). Both structs derive plain `Serialize` with no renames, so the fields are snake_case. The client reads `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cached_tokens` and `turns` from totals (runtime_threads.rs:5388-5390, 5425) and `key`, `turns`, `input_tokens` and `output_tokens` from each bucket (runtime_threads.rs:5494-5496, 5522). All of these are u64 or String, never null, so `fmtTokens` (src/lib/format.ts:1-7) always gets a number.
- Order. `buckets` is collected from a BTreeMap keyed by "YYYY-MM-DD" (runtime_threads.rs:10624-10625, 10724), so it comes back oldest first. The client's `.slice().reverse()` (SidePanels.tsx:142-144) then shows newest first, as intended.

What is wrong:
1. `turns` is not the number of user turns. The doc comment says it counts "provider-call usage records (parent turns plus child and compaction calls)" (runtime_threads.rs:5423-5425, 5521). aggregate_usage adds a record for:
   - the parent usage (10634-10645)
   - every `routed_usage` child, such as sub-agents and compaction (10663-10673, through 5896-5927)
   - every exact drop record (10674-10686)
   - every truncated or dropped fallback receipt (10691-10700)
   Each one increments `turns`: accumulate_runtime_usage_record (5803, 5842), accumulate_exact_runtime_usage_drop (5943, 5967) and accumulate_truncated_runtime_usage, which adds the whole dropped count (5867, 5887). One user prompt that starts sub-agents or triggers compaction therefore shows as several "Ходов", both in the summary tile (SidePanels.tsx:120) and in the per-day column (SidePanels.tsx:136, 148). Neither UsageTotals nor UsageBucket has a parent-turn-only counter (5387-5425, 5493-5522), so the client cannot read the right number from this endpoint.
2. A related issue the reviewer did not mention: day keys are in UTC. The key is `dispatched_at` or `created_at` (a `DateTime<Utc>`) formatted as `%Y-%m-%d` (runtime_threads.rs:5710-5713). For a user in UTC+3, work between 00:00 and 03:00 local time lands under the previous date in the "День" column (SidePanels.tsx:147).
verdict.fix:
No change is needed to the request: `GET /v1/usage?group_by=day` is correct as written.

In src/components/overlays/SidePanels.tsx:
- **Turn count:** Rename the "Ходов" label in both the tile (line 120) and the table header (line 136) to something like "Вызовов модели" ("model calls"). That matches what `totals.turns` and `buckets[].turns` actually count.
  - If the panel really needs user turns, it has to count them separately: walk `GET /v1/threads` and each thread's turns, and count parent turns per day. `/v1/usage` has no field for this.
  - Keep the tooltip or footnote that the number includes sub-agent and compaction calls.
- **Day dates:** Say in the header that the days are UTC ("День (UTC)"). Alternatively, rebuild the day buckets in local time on the client, which means requesting a different grouping or querying with per-day `since`/`until` RFC 3339 bounds at local midnight.
- **Optional:** Show `totals.dropped_usage_records` and treat `cost_complete` as "data incomplete", since `turns` may include dropped receipts that have no tokens.

verdict.evidence:
Verdict: partly stale, but the main defect is real and still unfixed. The working tree has uncommitted edits (git status shows threads.ts, useBootstrap.ts, app.ts and MessageList.tsx modified), so I checked against the current files, not HEAD.

1) MISMATCH 1 (stream.progress) is real at HEAD but already fixed in the working tree.
- Server: the progress frame is not an envelope. It is {schema_version, event, kind, thread_id, seq, state} with `state` at the top level and no payload (runtime_api.rs:9124-9135).
- HEAD: the client read `p.state`, which the git diff shows was removed.
- Now: threads.ts:236 reads `(ev as any).state`, and enqueueEvent reads the top-level `state` (threads.ts:534-542). useBootstrap no longer checks t.live; it uses isStreamLive (useBootstrap.ts:39-41, 47-48).
- Dedup lets the frame through even though its seq is at or below lastSeq (threads.ts:423), so `live` is set and the skeleton condition at MessageList.tsx:123 clears.

2) MISMATCH 2 is accurate but harmless.
- The runtime emits only "turn.completed" for terminal turns (emit_turn_completed_if_missing, runtime_threads.rs:9703-9731; call sites 9812, 14005, 18712). turn.failed and turn.interrupted appear only in exec_agent.rs:1282-1283 and the TUI outbox (tui/ui/event_loop.rs:3540-3542). Statuses are snake_case (runtime_threads.rs:758-767).
- So the turn.failed branch at threads.ts:252 (lastError) is dead. But the turn's error still arrives as turn.error (runtime_threads.rs:1636-1637) and is merged by mergeTurnRecord (threads.ts:166), and Turn.tsx:133 renders it.
- Refresh still works: useBootstrap.ts:78 includes turn.completed in TURN_END.
- New dead code in the working tree: the only `turn.lifecycle` emission sends {"status":"in_progress"} (runtime_threads.rs:16775-16781, the only occurrence). So the terminal-status branches at useBootstrap.ts:64-72 and threads.ts:258-260 never fire. This is harmless because turn.completed covers them.

3) CONFIRMED, not fixed: tail-limited replay silently loses history.
- Client: api.rs:129 still sends `replay_limit=4096`. A fresh open subscribes from 0: openStream resets the thread when `fresh` (or when it has no local copy), then subscribes from lastSeq (app.ts:99-107; called with fresh=true at app.ts:221, 231, 258).
- Server: ThreadEventsQuery takes replay_limit as Option<usize> (runtime_api.rs:1510-1515) and passes it to replay_events (runtime_api.rs:9084-9088). Some(limit) selects publish_tail_event_replay (runtime_threads.rs:4310-4314). That keeps only the newest `limit` events after since_seq and moves base_seq past the ones it drops (runtime_threads.rs:4450-4481). With None, publish_full_event_replay is used, which drops nothing and streams in batches of 256 (runtime_threads.rs:4410-4448).
- Every streamed agent_message chunk is persisted as its own item.delta event (runtime_threads.rs:16840-16857). Batching is only a 32 ms window (runtime_threads.rs:80). For a local model, 4096 events is therefore only a few long turns. Early turn.started/item.started events and user prompts (user_message items) are lost.
- The client has no gap detection. The only signals are the first progress frame's `seq` (= base_seq, runtime_api.rs:9246) and `previous_seq` on journal frames (runtime_api.rs:9198-9203, 9695-9703). The desktop app reads neither (grep finds no previous_seq in src or src-tauri/src).
- Seq numbers are global across threads (state.next_seq, runtime_threads.rs:4141-4144). So the gap test is "base_seq > requested since_seq", not "seq != previous+1".
- The server documents the intended pattern: GET /v1/threads/{id} returns ThreadDetail with latest_seq, pending_approvals and pending_user_inputs "without replaying events older than latest_seq" (runtime_threads.rs:5283-5303; route runtime_api.rs:2485; handler runtime_api.rs:7328-7337). The client already has threadViewFromDetail (threads.ts:476-507) but uses it only for export (export.ts:84-85).
verdict.fix:
1) Opening a thread (app.ts openStream, lines 99-111):
- When opening fresh or with no local copy, first call `api.request("GET", "/v1/threads/${id}")`.
- Seed the store with threadViewFromDetail(detail), but set live=false and streamState="connecting" instead of live=true / "closed".
- Then call `api.subscribe(id, detail.latest_seq)`. The stream then carries only new events, and pending approvals and user inputs come from the snapshot.
- Do the same in reloadThread (app.ts:229-236).
- Minimal alternative: remove `replay_limit=4096` from the URL at api.rs:129. With no replay_limit the server does a full lossless replay (runtime_threads.rs:4410-4448), but long threads then re-send every item.delta.

2) Gap detection in src-tauri/src/api.rs stream_loop (lines 119-191):
- Remember the since_seq used for each connection.
- On the first stream.progress frame, parse `seq` from the JSON. Alternatively, use `previous_seq` from the first journal frame.
- If that value is greater than the requested since_seq, the server dropped history. Emit `emit_state(app, thread_id, "gap", ...)` and have the UI re-seed from GET /v1/threads/{id} (step 1).
- Do not compare seq with previous_seq+1: seq is global across threads (runtime_threads.rs:4141-4144).

3) Cleanup:
- threads.ts:252: set lastError on `env.event === "turn.completed" && p.turn.status === "failed"`, using p.turn.error. Otherwise remove the dead turn.failed/turn.interrupted/turn.canceled cases.
- Remove the terminal-status branches of turn.lifecycle (useBootstrap.ts:64-72, threads.ts:258-260). The runtime only emits status "in_progress" there (runtime_threads.rs:16775-16781).
- No change is needed for stream.progress: threads.ts:236 and 534-542 already read the top-level `state`.
